Early 3DGS implementations stored millions of Gaussians, leading to bandwidth bottlenecks during sorting and rasterization.
Hierarchical and multi-resolution techniques, inspired by point cloud compression and Nanite-style virtual geometry, were developed to mitigate this.

The specific "K-wise moment-matched" approach provides a mathematically rigorous way to merge splats with minimal visual error, while simpler averaging methods offer computational efficiency for real-time LOD generation.
